column1: # Missed mutants a person has judged, so the nightly report can set them
# apart from new ones. scripts/mutants/report.py reads this file.
# kind: "equivalent" (the mutant cannot change any result, so no test can
# catch it) or "elsewhere" (a test outside the mutated crate catches it,
# usually a satd/tests integration test, which cargo-mutants does not run).
# A row names a mutant by its source line rather than its line number, so it
# survives code moving above it: file, the line's text with its indentation
# trimmed, the mutant's column in that trimmed text, and the mutation as
# cargo-mutants describes it after the location. When the line itself
# changes the row stops matching and the mutant is reported as new again,
# for a person to judge afresh; the report lists rows that match no line.
# A row must name exactly one mutant (check with `cargo mutants --list` on
# its file). The report never matches a mutant whose line text appears more
# than once in its function, so a copy of a known line added later is
# reported as new rather than hidden by the row. For a mutant outside any
# function (a constant, say) the line must be unique in its file.
# Tab-separated: file, column, mutation, kind, why, line.
